clue: Almost every house has a black, beige, or white cylindrical 'Rotoplas' water tank sitting on the flat roof.
The backs of the street signs are painted completely black.
The center lines on the road are entirely white; they do not use yellow lines to separate oncoming traffic.
Concrete utility poles feature a distinct design with round holes running up the middle, and sometimes have a painted red, yellow, and blue band.
The Cyrillic alphabet includes the unique letters 'ң', 'ө', and 'ү', which you won't see in standard Russian.
Language uses letters with 'ogonek' hooks at the bottom (ą, ę, į, ų) rather than macrons (ā, ē, ī, ū).
License plates often feature a distinct black dot squarely in the middle of the alphanumeric sequence.
